text:
yoel: heads up - admission webhook started rejecting a subset of canaries this morning with "provenance missing" and cosign verify rpc PermissionDenied. Pasting a log snippet.

sasha: can you drop the cosign output?

yoel: ```
$ cosign verify --key ksm://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/artifacts/cryptoKeys/artifact-signer gcr.io/redwood/service-api@sha256:deadbeef
Error: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = permission denied for KMS signer
```

patrick: hmm. I didn't touch that key. We did roll an identity-alias rename in infra (PR#1342) to migrate from service principal email to identity alias for the signer SA. Maybe the alias didn't get an IAM binding.

build-team: we also changed the artifact publisher in CI to call cosign via the identity alias URI (ksm://.../identities/alias-artifact-signer) yesterday. Could be a mismatch between key path and binding.

attest-bot: AttestEvent: envelope_missing image=gcr.io/redwood/service-api:2026-07-02-rc1 status=missing time=2026-07-02T09:12:10Z

security-bot: AuditEvent: IAMPolicyChange project=redwood actor=ops-sync@redwood change=removed roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeySigner member=serviceAccount:artifact-signer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com time=2026-07-02T08:58:03Z

patrick: ops-sync removed the binding during the daily policy reconcile because the member email no longer matched after the alias migration. That left the identity alias in a limbo: CI published signatures with the alias identity but the KMS key had no binding for the alias. The result: envelopes may have been created locally by CI but KMS refused verification.

yoel: runtime behavior question - do nodes reject images permanently or is there a fallback to previous tag? We had a few pods stuck Pending.

sre-oncall: admission is configured fail-closed. For staging canaries we have a 1-hour automatic fallback to previous image tag; for prod it's manual. Pending means the pod won't start until image passes checks. We prevented prod impact.

build-team: mitigation plan: (1) re-add IAM binding for the identity alias and the original service account email to the KMS key; (2) re-run attest check for the affected digests; (3) if any artifacts were signed with a destroyed/retired key version -> rebuild + sign via CI pipeline using canonical signer URI.

patrick: exact gcloud to add alias binding: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/artifacts/cryptoKeys/artifact-signer \
  --member="principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456/locations/global/identityAwareProxyNames/alias-artifact-signer" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeySigner"
```

patrick: and re-add email binding to be safe: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/artifacts/cryptoKeys/artifact-signer \
  --member="serviceAccount:artifact-signer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeySigner"
```

attest-bot: ActionLog: iam_binding_added actor=patrick@redwood target=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/artifacts/cryptoKeys/artifact-signer time=2026-07-02T10:05:11Z

build-team: re-run of attest job shows cosign verify passing for 7/8 digests; one digest still fails with "public key not found for key version" -> that artifact was signed with a key version we retired and destroyed during an earlier rotation. We'll need to rebuild that artifact.

security-bot: AuditEvent: KMSKeyVersionDestroy actor=infra-admin@redwood key=artifact-signer version=3 time=2026-06-25T04:02:12Z

build-team: queueing a rebuild of the single affected image using the canonical pipeline builder (builders/regenerate/198). CI will sign with KMS URI ksm://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/artifacts/cryptoKeys/artifact-signer and upload attestation envelope to gs://redwood-attest/2026-07-02.

yoel: can we regenerate attestations from registry blobs instead of rebuilding? The layer blobs still exist in registry.

build-team: for the destroyed key-version case, regen won't help because signature was produced with a destroyed private key and cannot be verified. But for missing envelopes we can regenerate attestations from blobs if the attestation SA has storage access.

security-bot: AuditEvent: IAMPolicyChange actor=ops-sync@redwood change=removed roles/storage.objectViewer member=serviceAccount:attest-uploader@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com time=2026-07-02T08:56:01Z

patrick: ops-sync also removed the attest uploader's storage role. That explains missing envelopes for a different subset. I'll re-add storage.objectViewer to attest-uploader and identity alias signer binding.

attest-bot: ActionLog: iam_binding_added actor=patrick@redwood target=project=redwood role=roles/storage.objectViewer member=serviceAccount:attest-uploader@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com time=2026-07-02T10:10:40Z

build-team: regen job completed; attestation envelopes uploaded. Rebuild job for destroyed-key artifact finished and signed by CI. cosign verify and admission checks now pass for all canary images.

yoel: verified locally and in staging. canary moving to 5% then 25%.

sre-oncall: monitoring metrics - no increase in errors at 25% after 20m.

patrick: postmortem action items: (1) add ops-sync allowlist for identity-alias and for artifact attester SAs; (2) CI preflight to assert KMS bindings + attest uploader storage access after key rotations or identity migrations; (3) builder test to ensure deterministic tar ordering (prevent unnecessary layer churn); (4) runbook update: if provenance missing -> do not relax admission gates, attempt regen if attest SA has storage access, else rebuild; (5) add an automation to re-provision KMS bindings when identity-alias migrations are performed.

yoel: logging these as infra/PR#1356 (ops-sync allowlist), ci/PR#678 (preflight), builders/PR#720 (deterministic ordering), runbook/PR#44. tagging owners: @patrick infra, @build-team builders, @sasha security. thanks all :thumbsup:
